description.value: The study examined how chronic and acute exercise affect neuronal responses to visual food cues in healthy overweight/obese adults using repeated-measures fMRI before and after a six-month exercise intervention.

spans.text: The objective of this study was to examine the effects of exercise training and acute exercise on the neuronal response to food cues as well as eating behaviors.

value: Reduced responses to visual food cues following chronic exercise compared to baseline were observed in the bilateral parietal cortices, left insula and visual cortex.
Chronic exercise resulted in diminished activation in the insula, parietal cortices, and visual cortex, suggesting that the salience of the food cues is reduced with exercise.
